Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has directed authorities to ensure round-the-clock operations at all ports across Bangladesh to facilitate trade and speed up import and export activities.
The directive came during a high-level meeting with the country's leading business leaders and industrialists at the Prime Minister's Office in Tejgaon on Saturday.
Briefing reporters after the meeting, Prime Minister's Adviser and spokesperson Mahdi Amin said the decision followed a proposal from the private sector to introduce 24-hour commercial operations at Chittagong Port and Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
"The private sector proposed introducing 24-hour services for import and export activities at Chittagong Port and Dhaka airport. The prime minister immediately directed the authorities to take the necessary steps," Mahdi said.
He said all relevant government agencies would work together to ensure that every port in Bangladesh provides 24-hour services in the coming days.
"The move will make import and export activities faster and more efficient," he added.
Mahdi said the meeting also featured extensive discussions on challenges facing the private sector, existing bottlenecks, and the country's overall investment climate.
According to him, the discussions also focused on attracting more investment to the country's economic zones, including those under the Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority (BEZA) and the Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA), while simplifying existing procedures.
Relevant ministers, state ministers, advisers, and heads of various government agencies also shared their views during the meeting, he said.
Highlighting the government's commitment to supporting the private sector, Mahdi said the administration aims to establish a governance framework under the prime minister's leadership that provides strong policy support for businesses.
"We have presented a pro-business, pro-investment budget, and we will implement those policies. The main objective is to harness Bangladesh's demographic dividend by creating more employment and self-employment opportunities for young people and women," he said.
Quoting one of the prime minister's slogans, Mahdi said: "The prime minister always says, 'We will work, we will build the nation, Bangladesh comes first.' Guided by that principle, today's discussion prioritized Bangladesh's interests."
He added that representatives of the private sector welcomed the government's efforts to implement people-friendly policies, including a people-friendly budget.
Mahdi said business leaders expressed satisfaction over the government's immediate decisions on several policy proposals.
"The objective of the discussion is to make doing business easier, encourage greater investment-driven growth, and create more employment opportunities across Bangladesh," he said.

item.title: Inside RAB's mirror room: 29 cells, hidden 'death chambers'
item.description:
Judges of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT)-1 on Friday inspected the former Task Force for Interrogation (TFI) facility inside the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB)-1 headquarters, where prosecutors allege people were secretly detained, tortured and, in some cases, disappeared during the Awami League government's tenure.
The inspection offered the tribunal its first direct look inside what investigators describe as one of the country's most significant alleged secret detention centres, where prosecutors say structural alterations were made after the political transition in an attempt to conceal evidence.
The three-member tribunal, accompanied by Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam and members of the prosecution team, toured the two-storey facility, widely known as the "mirror room," located beside the armoury inside the RAB-1 compound in Uttara.
According to the prosecution, investigators initially struggled to match survivors' accounts with the existing layout because sections of the facility had allegedly been walled off after August 5, 2024.
Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam said investigators later demolished newly built walls and uncovered 22 concealed detention rooms, bringing the total number of cells inside the facility to 29.
"The prison could not initially be found to match the victims' descriptions because a camouflage had been created," he said.
"After removing the walls, we found the hidden rooms. Beneath them we also found what were known as death cells. The entire facility is horrific."
According to prosecutors, the building contains 29 permanent detention cells, including seven extremely narrow cells measuring roughly two by four feet, which they described as "death cells."
The prosecution further alleged that when detainee numbers increased, additional victims were held in makeshift canvas-partitioned spaces inside the building.
Investigators also identified three soundproof interrogation rooms, which prosecutors say contained equipment allegedly used to torture detainees, including a motorised rotating steel chair, devices capable of administering electric shocks, ceiling suspension mechanisms and iron restraint beds.
The prosecution alleged that victims were subjected to prolonged physical and psychological torture in attempts to extract confessions.
During the inspection, prosecutors also pointed to photographs allegedly displayed inside interrogation rooms depicting severely mutilated victims, which they said were intended to intimidate detainees.
According to the prosecution, the TFI facility, officially established for interrogating suspects, was transformed into a secret detention centre during the Awami League government between 2009 and 2024 and operated under RAB's Intelligence Wing.
The prosecution alleged that people with different political affiliations and opinions were secretly detained there, with some later shown arrested in regular criminal cases while others allegedly disappeared or were killed.
Aminul Islam said more than 250 alleged victims of enforced disappearance or suspected extrajudicial killing linked to the facility remain unaccounted for.
He said the missing include former BNP leader Ilias Ali and another disappearance victim identified as Sumon.
The tribunal is currently hearing crimes against humanity allegations relating to enforced disappearances and torture at the facility. One of the complainants is Barrister Mir Ahmed Bin Kashem, who has alleged he was secretly detained there.
The chief prosecutor said those responsible not only for operating the facility but also for allegedly attempting to destroy or conceal evidence after the change in government would also face legal proceedings.
The allegations made during Friday's inspection form part of an ongoing investigation and judicial process before the International Crimes Tribunal.

item.title: Mahdi Amin: US voices confidence in Bangladesh PM's leadership
item.description:
The United States has expressed strong confidence in the leadership of Bangladesh's elected Prime Minister, praising the country's return to stability and democratic progress, Prime Minister's Office (PMO) Spokesperson and Adviser Mahdi Amin said on Saturday.
He made the remarks while briefing reporters at the Prime Minister's Office following a meeting between visiting US President Donald Trump's Special Envoy for South and Central Asia and US ambassador to India Sergio Gor and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
"The United States said Bangladesh has regained stability under the Prime Minister's leadership and is moving forward on a strong democratic path," Mahdi Amin said. "It also commended the policies the Prime Minister has pursued over the past five months."
He said the meeting also focused on further strengthening the longstanding and multifaceted partnership between Bangladesh and the United States through deeper economic engagement.
According to Mahdi Amin, the two sides discussed expanding US investment, increasing bilateral trade, creating more employment through American companies operating in Bangladesh and exploring policy support the government could provide to facilitate greater investment.
The discussions also covered ways to boost exports and imports between the two countries, he added. Mahdi Amin announced that around 45 senior executives and business leaders from nearly 25 leading US companies are expected to visit Bangladesh by the end of next week, describing the visit as an important step towards increasing American investment in the country.
During the visit, the delegation will hold a series of meetings with officials from key ministries and government agencies, while a separate meeting with the Prime Minister is also scheduled, he said.
Describing the talks as cordial and constructive, Mahdi Amin said the discussions were expected to add a new dimension to Bangladesh-US relations.
"We hope to expand trade with the United States, attract greater American investment and create more employment opportunities in Bangladesh," he said.

item.title: DSCC showcases fridges, TVs, sofas recovered from Dhaka drains
item.description:
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) on Saturday staged an unusual awareness procession featuring refrigerators, televisions, sofas, mattresses, polythene and plastic waste recovered from drains to demonstrate how indiscriminate waste disposal contributes to waterlogging and environmental pollution in the capital.
The "Waste Procession" was inaugurated at Shahbagh by DSCC Administrator Md Abdus Salam, alongside the launch of the corporation's monthly "Cleaning Day," observed simultaneously across all 75 wards.
Speaking at the event, the DSCC administrator said Dhaka cannot become a clean and green city without greater public awareness and civic responsibility.
"If everyone fulfills their responsibilities, a large part of the city's waterlogging, waste management and environmental pollution problems can be controlled," he said.
Urging residents not to blame the city corporation alone for waterlogging, he said citizens also have a responsibility to dispose of waste properly.
"Even a single polythene bag or a discarded mattress can block a drain and cause waterlogging across an entire neighborhood," he said, calling on residents not to dump waste into drains.
Abdus Salam said changing public behavior is essential if Dhaka is to shed its reputation as one of the world's most polluted cities.
"If we do not become conscious ourselves, it will not be possible to protect Dhaka," he added.
He also said dustbins are being reinstalled across the city under the prime minister's directive after many previously installed bins were stolen. He urged business owners to place waste bins in front of their establishments, saying there is no excuse for indiscriminate dumping.
The administrator announced that a special crash program on mosquito control and waste management will be carried out on the first Saturday of every month across all 75 DSCC wards.
Alongside routine cleaning activities, the initiative will focus on clearing clogged drains and cleaning neglected areas. He also invited social, voluntary and political organizations to participate.
Highlighting the importance of environmental protection, Abdus Salam stressed the need for extensive tree planting, saying it is essential to reduce carbon dioxide levels and increase oxygen.
He also praised volunteers from Bidyanondo Foundation for their community service, saying a cleaner, more livable Dhaka requires collective efforts from citizens, the media and civil society.
Following the inauguration, participants marched through several roads carrying waste recovered from drains to demonstrate the consequences of improper waste disposal. They also distributed awareness leaflets explaining the causes of waterlogging, proper waste management practices and the harmful effects of plastic pollution.
DSCC Chief Executive Officer Md Khairur Rahman attended the event as a special guest. Bidyanondo Foundation Executive Director Md Jamal Uddin, environmental activists, students, volunteers, DSCC officials and media representatives were also present.

item.title: Road crashes killed 1,384 in Dhaka since 2020
item.description:
A total of 1,384 people were killed and 2,488 others injured in 1,849 road crashes across the capital between January 2020 and July 2026, according to data released by the Road Safety Foundation on Saturday.
The analysis found that 1,034 of those killed were men (74.71%), 219 were women (15.82%), and 131 were children (9.46%).
Year-wise data showed that 126 people were killed and 233 injured in 124 crashes in 2020. The figures rose to 141 deaths and 247 injuries in 137 crashes in 2021, followed by 256 deaths and 324 injuries in 268 crashes in 2022.
In 2023, 249 people were killed and 335 injured in 296 crashes. The following year, 246 people died and 482 were injured in 394 crashes. In 2025, 229 people were killed and 511 injured in 407 crashes. Up to July 2026, 137 people had been killed and 356 injured in 223 crashes.
Of those killed, 592 (42.77%) were pedestrians, 536 (38.72%) were motorcyclists, and 256 (18.49%) were drivers or passengers of buses, rickshaws, CNG-run auto-rickshaws, and other vehicles.
Most fatalities occurred at night, accounting for 519 deaths (37.5%). The remaining deaths were recorded in the morning (258), afternoon (195), evening (174), early morning (142), and at dusk (96).
Heavy vehicles—including trucks, covered vans, pickups, tankers, and garbage trucks—were involved in the highest proportion of crashes (33.25%), followed by motorcycles (26%), buses (21.75%), auto-rickshaws, CNG-run auto-rickshaws, and legunas (12.73%), and microbuses, private cars, and jeeps (6.25%).
The Road Safety Foundation said road crashes occur more frequently at night and in the morning in the capital. It attributed the trend to heavy goods vehicles traveling at high speeds during nighttime due to the absence of bypass roads, exposing pedestrians to greater risk while crossing roads.
The organization also blamed chronic traffic congestion, inadequate road infrastructure, mixed traffic, encroached footpaths, a shortage of usable footbridges, and poor road-user awareness for the high number of crashes and fatalities.
It identified Jatrabari, Demra, Mohammadpur, Kuril World Road, and Airport Road as major crash hotspots.
The foundation recommended introducing company-based bus services through route rationalization to improve discipline in Dhaka's public transport system. It also called for coordinated action by the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA), Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC), Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority (DTCA), the two city corporations, and the traffic police.

Fit-again Liton boosts Bangladesh squad for Australia Tests
item.description:
Bangladesh received a boost Saturday as experienced wicketkeeper-batsman Liton Das joined the squad for two Tests in Australia after recovering from a calf injury.
Liton was added to the squad for the first Test in Darwin on August 13-17, the Bangladesh Cricket Board said.
The 31-year-old had been sidelined since June with a left calf injury and was initially ruled out of the opening Test of the two-match series.
His return provides timely reinforcement for Bangladesh, who have been hit by injury ahead of their first Test tour of Australia in 23 years.
Fast bowler Nahid Rana has been ruled out of the series with a side strain, while left-arm seamer Shoriful Islam was not selected for the opening Test because of a hamstring injury.
Bangladesh will warm up for the Tests with match against a Cricket Australia XI in Darwin from August 6-8.
The second and final Test will be played in Mackay from August 22-26.

item.title: DU launches July uprising graffiti restoration drive
item.description:
Dhaka University on Saturday launched a three-day campaign to restore the July graffiti displayed across its campus, aiming to preserve the murals created during the July–August 2024 mass uprising.
Vice-Chancellor Professor ABM Obaidul Islam inaugurated the program at the main gate of the vice-chancellor's residence.
The restoration work will continue through Sunday and Monday along the route from the vice-chancellor's residence to Rokeya Hall, with registered students and artists taking part.
Speaking at the inauguration, DU VC said the July graffiti serves as a reminder of the "misrule of the fallen fascist government" and that the restoration initiative is intended to preserve the memory of the oppression and persecution depicted in the murals.
He said: "During July and August, patriotic students painted the walls with graffiti depicting the marks of Sheikh Hasina's oppression, persecution, and vengeance. These graffiti now stand as living history for the nation."
The vice-chancellor said the murals would continue to remind future generations of the events of July–August 2024 and help keep the anti-fascist spirit alive.
He also urged people to remain vigilant against the return of fascism and called on citizens to support the government's efforts to build a discrimination-free society.
Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Academic) Professor Abdus Salam, Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Administration) Professor Mohammed Almujaddade Alfasane, Treasurer Professor M Jahangir Alam Chowdhury, were present at the time, among others.
As part of events marking the second anniversary of the July mass uprising, a discussion will be held at 7:30pm on Saturday at the Amar Ekushey Hall auditorium. The VC will attend as the chief guest, while Sarjis Alam, chief organizer (Northern Region) of the National Citizen Party (NCP), will attend as the special guest.

item.title: Businessman dies after assault in Khilgaon
item.description:
A 40-year-old businessman died after being beaten allegedly by a group of unidentified assailants in the capital's Khilgaon area, police said on Saturday
The deceased was identified as Kamruzzaman Khan Dipu, who ran a water supply business. He was the son of Md Sams Uddin and a resident of 721/1/A, Block C, Khilgaon, said Sub-Inspector (SI) Sumon Mia of Khilgaon Police Station.
Police recovered the body from Mugda General Hospital around 10pm on Friday. After completing the required legal formalities, the body was sent to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) morgue, where an autopsy was conducted on Saturday.
According to police, witnesses said 10 to 12 unidentified men assaulted Dipu around 7pm on July 29 before leaving him critically injured near the Khilgaon Rail Gate.
He was first taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors advised immediate admission to the intensive care unit (ICU). However, no ICU bed was available, and his family could not afford treatment at a private hospital. They later took him home.
His condition deteriorated, and he was taken to Mugda General Hospital around 7:45pm on Friday, where the duty doctor declared him dead.
Police said an investigation was underway, and legal action will be taken based on its findings.

item.title: Swapon: Humanitarian philosophy essential to rebuild nation after fascism
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Jahir Uddin Swapon on Saturday said the chapter of ousting fascism has ended and the country must now focus on rebuilding the state, strengthening democratic institutions and fostering a society rooted in humanity, tolerance and mutual respect.
Speaking as the chief guest at a discussion and photo exhibition titled "Bangladesh in the Face of Bullets, Fascism Came to an End" at the National Press Club, Swapon said the movement had achieved its objectives of restoring democracy and ensuring people's voting rights.
"The phase of toppling fascism is over. Now is the time to build the country," he said. "The movement was aimed at restoring democracy and securing the people's right to vote. We must now rebuild the state, strengthen democratic institutions and work together to fulfil the aspirations of the people."
The minister said the country's journey towards restoring democracy had been shaped by a prolonged popular movement. While crediting the people with the success of the movement, he said BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman had provided leadership and strategic direction from abroad.
Swapon said Tarique Rahman never claimed personal credit for the mass uprising, instead consistently describing it as a victory of the people and working to keep pro-democracy forces united throughout the movement.
He said two slogans popularised by Tarique Rahman"If you are afraid, you are finished; if you stand up, you are Bangladesh" and "The country's future will be decided on the streets" injected fresh momentum into the movement, which culminated in the August 5 mass uprising.
The minister said that with the national election concluded, the country now needs politics centred on nation-building rather than confrontation. He stressed the need to strengthen democratic practices, ensure an effective parliamentary system and uphold responsible governance to meet public expectations.
He said that while political movements might become a profession for some, their struggle had always been aimed at restoring democracy, safeguarding voting rights and building an independent and sovereign Bangladesh. With those goals achieved, he added, the focus should now shift to development and state-building.
Highlighting the importance of preserving the history of the anti-fascist movement, Swapon said photographs taken by photojournalists would remain enduring records of the struggle for democracy for future generations.

item.title: IOM deputy DG arrives in Dhaka on four-day visit
item.description:
The International Organization for Migration's (IOM) Deputy Director General for Operations, Ugochi Daniels , arrived in Dhaka on Saturday on a four-day official visit to Bangladesh.
She was received at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport by IOM Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific Iori Kato , United Nations Resident Coordinator in Bangladesh Carol Flore-Smereczniak , and IOM Chief of Mission in Bangladesh Dr Laura Tomm Bonde .
During the visit, Daniels is scheduled to meet senior government officials, UN partners, donors, and communities supported by IOM.
She will also attend the launch of Bangladesh's National Action Plan 2026–2030 for the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM).
As part of her itinerary, Daniels will travel to Cox's Bazar and Madaripur to engage with stakeholders on migration governance, climate mobility, labor migration, protection, and humanitarian response.

item.title: NAAB holds ‘Strategic Engagement Meeting 2026’
item.description:
The Netherlands Alumni Association of Bangladesh (NAAB) Strategic Engagement Meeting 2026 was held on July 30 at the KIB (Krishibid Institution Bangladesh) Complex.
A total of 45 registered NAAB members participated in this important strategic event organized by the association.
The meeting aimed to bring together NAAB members to discuss the association's future direction and identify strategic priorities for strengthening NAAB's role, expanding member engagement, and enhancing its contribution to Bangladesh–Netherlands relations.
During the meeting, members shared valuable ideas, suggestions, and constructive feedback on how to further strengthen and advance NAAB in the coming years.
The event featured lively and interactive discussions, with enthusiastic participation and strong commitment from all attendees toward building a stronger, more vibrant, and sustainable NAAB.
Dr Kamruzzaman Kaiser, president of NAAB, formally inaugurated the meeting by welcoming all participants.
In his opening remarks, he encouraged members to actively participate in the open discussion and share their ideas, experiences, and suggestions for the future development of the Association.
Among the distinguished participants was Akhtar Ahmed, senior secretary of the Election Commission Secretariat and a registered NAAB member.
He shared his personal perspectives and valuable recommendations, emphasizing the importance of making NAAB a more vibrant and active organization through greater engagement and participation of its members.
AR Malik Seeds Pvt Ltd sponsored flower seeds for all participants.
A representative from the company delivered a brief presentation on flower cultivation and production technology.
Participants were delighted to receive the seeds and appreciated the initiative.
NAAB requested all recipients to cultivate the flowers and share their progress through the NAAB WhatsApp group.
The cultivation results will be reviewed and recognized at a future NAAB event.
This initiative was conceived and implemented by Dr M Golam Mahboob, chief scientific officer, BARC, and Dr Naeema Jihan Zinia, managing partner, EnvSoL.
The meeting concluded on a highly positive note, with participants expressing their appreciation for the opportunity to exchange ideas and contribute to NAAB's future strategic direction.
Everyone also enjoyed the refreshments and dinner, and highly appreciated the excellent hospitality and overall arrangements provided by the KIB.

Indian passenger held in suspected gold smuggling at Shah Amanat Airport
item.description:
Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate (CIID) officials have detained an Indian passenger at Chattogram’s Shah Amanat International Airport after recovering capsule-like objects containing gold.
Acting on a tip-off, a team from the CIID regional office in Chattogram intercepted the passenger after he crossed the green channel at the airport on Saturday morning.
The passenger, identified as Thamim Ansari, arrived from Sharjah in the United Arab Emirates on Air Arabia flight G9-526, which landed at 6:58 am.
During a body search, officials recovered capsule-shaped packets containing gold concealed inside his underwear.
Authorities said the exact quantity and purity of the gold are being determined with the assistance of a certified goldsmith after removing the packing materials.
The recovered gold is estimated to be worth around Tk 1 crore, officials said.
CIID said legal action is being taken against the passenger under the Customs Act, while steps are also underway to file a criminal case in connection with the smuggling attempt.
The agency said it would continue intelligence surveillance and enforcement drives to prevent the smuggling of gold and other contraband through the country’s international airports.

item.title: State minister: New Dhaka–Cox's Bazar Train pair to launch this month
item.description:
State Minister for Railways Habibur Rashid has announced that a new pair of intercity trains will be launched on the Dhaka–Cox's Bazar route later this month to meet growing passenger demand and ease ticket shortages.
The announcement came during his visit to the Cox's Bazar Railway Station on Saturday morning.
The state minister said the number of passengers and tourists travelling to Cox's Bazar has been increasing steadily, prompting the government to expand rail services and modernize passenger facilities.
He expressed hope that the new train pair would significantly reduce passenger suffering, ease ticket pressure and ensure a more comfortable, convenient and timely journey on the route.
Rashid also said the government plans to transform the Cox's Bazar Railway Station into an international-standard, tourism-friendly rail hub.
As part of this initiative, the full operation and management of the station will be entrusted to a private organization to ensure efficient and high-quality services.
During the visit, the state minister inspected various sections of the station and reviewed passenger services, infrastructure, cleanliness, security arrangements and overall operational activities.
He instructed the concerned officials to expedite the full opening of the station and ensure international-standard services for passengers.
Cox's Bazar Sadar MP Lutfur Rahman, senior railway officials and officials of the Cox's Bazar Railway Station were present during the visit.

item.title: Tourist dies after falling from parasailing ride at Cox's Bazar beach
item.description:
A tourist was killed after falling from a parasailing ride into the sea at Dariyanagar Beach in Cox's Bazar.

The victim was identified as Akshar Shouvik Roy, 30, son of Shekhar Roy of Sir Iqbal Road in the Baniakhamar area of Khulna City Corporation.

The incident occurred around 12:30 pm on Saturday at Dariyanagar Beach along the Cox's Bazar–Teknaf Marine Drive.

The parasailing service was being operated by Fly Air Sea Sports Parasailing, a company that has been running the activity at the beach for more than a decade.

Although tourists have reportedly been injured in similar incidents in the past, no action has been taken against the operator.

Authorities had recently banned parasailing because of adverse weather conditions, but the company allegedly continued operating.

Repeated attempts to contact the company's owner, Mohammad Farid of Baharchhara in Cox's Bazar town, were unsuccessful as he did not answer his phone.

According to police and witnesses, Shouvik and eight friends had travelled from Khulna to Cox's Bazar. Around noon, he bought a Tk 2,000 ticket and prepared for the ride.

Shortly after takeoff, when the parasail had reached an altitude of approximately 300–400 feet, he suddenly became detached and fell into the Bay of Bengal.

Employees of the parasailing company later recovered him from the water and took him to Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital, where phycisians declared him dead.

One of Shouvik's friends expressed anger over the lack of emergency response.

"When Shouvik fell into the sea, there was no rescue arrangement. We did not see any lifeguards at Dariyanagar. A speedboat eventually rescued him and took him to the hospital, but by then it was too late," he said.

Confirming the incident, Sheikh Mohammad Ali, officer in charge of Cox's Bazar Sadar Model Police Station, said the body had been sent to the hospital morgue.

He added that authorities were investigating both the death and the operation of parasailing services despite adverse weather conditions.

Cox's Bazar Deputy Commissioner Md A Mannan said all parasailing activities, including those at Dariyanagar, had been suspended three days earlier because of rough weather.

"All parasailing activities had been banned. However, some operators continued the service without the administration's knowledge. Today's death is tragic. We are investigating the matter. No permission was given by the administration to operate parasailing," he told Prothom Alo.

Sifat Saifullah, supervisor of private rescue service Sea Safe Lifeguards, said 27 lifeguards patrol the five-kilometre stretch between Kolatoli and Laboni Point.

However, there are no lifeguards or rescue divers along the 115-kilometre coastline from Dariyanagar south to Himchhari, Inani and Teknaf.

Safety concerns raised

Nazrul Islam, member secretary of the Cox's Bazar Citizens'' Movement, alleged that several operators continue to offer parasailing at different beach locations while ignoring safety regulations.

Tourists are frequently injured after falling from parasailing rides. Today, one person has died.

None of the operators has international-standard safety measures, trained operators, rescue boats or first-aid facilities. These risky activities should remain suspended until safety standards are verified.

Dhaka resident Kamal Uddin, who had come to try parasailing, explained that the parasail is pulled by a speedboat using a heavy rope.

According to him, the rider controls ascent and descent, but many lose control while airborne, increasing the risk of falling. He added that the lack of a rapid rescue system makes such accidents fatal.

Local residents said a female tourist was blown into a casuarina grove while parasailing at Dariyanagar beach on 30 August last year, remaining stranded in the treetops for a prolonged period before being rescued.

The following day, the district administration temporarily suspended all parasailing activities.

Earlier, on 20 May, 2025, another tourist was injured after falling into the sea during a parasailing ride at the same beach.

item.title: AIDS 2026 Conference ends with scientific hope, funding uncertainty
item.description:
The world's largest HIV conference concluded in Rio de Janeiro on Friday with a clear message: while scientific advances have brought humanity closer than ever to ending AIDS, declining global funding now poses the greatest threat to achieving that goal.
After six days of scientific presentations, policy debates and community discussions, delegates at the 26th International AIDS Conference (AIDS 2026) celebrated major advances in HIV prevention and treatment while warning that shrinking financial support could reverse decades of progress.
More than 7,000 researchers, policymakers, health professionals, activists and people living with HIV from over 175 countries attended the conference under the theme "Rethink. Rebuild. Rise."
The overriding conclusion was that science is no longer the biggest barrier to ending HIV; equitable access is.
Researchers presented promising data on long-acting HIV prevention medicines, simplified treatment strategies and next-generation therapies that could dramatically reduce new infections and improve treatment adherence. Experts described the findings as the most significant advances since antiretroviral therapy transformed HIV from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition.
Delegates, however, cautioned that these breakthroughs will have limited impact unless governments, donors and pharmaceutical companies ensure affordable and equitable access.
Incoming International AIDS Society (IAS) President Professor Kenneth Ngure of Kenya said scientific discoveries change lives only when they are translated into policies, financing and health services that reach the people who need them most.
Outlining his vision for the IAS, Ngure pledged to champion science, equity and the next generation of researchers while working to ensure that innovation benefits all countries, not just the wealthiest.
Despite the optimism surrounding these advances, concerns over funding dominated discussions throughout the conference.
Researchers, UN agencies and civil society organizations warned that the global HIV response is facing one of its most challenging financial periods in decades following significant cuts to international assistance, particularly from the United States.
Community organizations in several countries have already begun scaling back HIV prevention, testing and outreach services, raising fears that hard-won gains could be reversed.
New estimates presented during the conference showed that around 1.2 million people acquired HIV and 570,000 died from AIDS-related illnesses worldwide in 2025.
Experts warned those figures could rise if investment continues to decline.
The conference also highlighted how quickly HIV epidemics can expand when prevention programs weaken, citing Fiji as a stark example.
Researchers described Fiji as one of the world's fastest-growing HIV outbreaks, with new diagnoses rising sharply over the past five years, driven largely by injecting drug use. They urged the expansion of harm reduction measures, including needle and syringe programs, opioid substitution therapy and community-led interventions.
Throughout the week, speakers stressed that biomedical innovation alone will not end AIDS.
Success, they said, will also depend on protecting human rights, reducing stigma, strengthening community-led organizations and ensuring that key populations remain at the center of the response.
The discussions also carried important lessons for Bangladesh. Although the country remains a low-prevalence setting, much of its HIV prevention program—particularly services for people who inject drugs and other key populations—continues to rely on international donor support.
Experts said declining external financing makes greater domestic investment increasingly important to sustain prevention efforts and protect past achievements.
The conference also underscored the need for stronger collaboration between scientists, governments and communities, arguing that scientific breakthroughs have little value if they remain confined to laboratories instead of reaching the people who need them.
As the conference concluded, the International AIDS Society entered a new chapter with Kenneth Ngure assuming its presidency.
Ngure said the next phase of the global HIV response must focus not only on generating scientific evidence but also on translating discoveries into policies that improve lives through equitable access, stronger partnerships and investment in young researchers.
Delegates also looked ahead to the IAS Conference on HIV Science (IAS 2027), scheduled to be held in Geneva, Switzerland, from July 12 to 15, 2027, where scientists and policymakers will assess whether the commitments made in Rio have translated into tangible progress.

item.title: No respite for Dhaka consumers as food prices soar
item.description:
As households struggle to cope with rising living costs, there is little sign of relief in Dhaka's kitchen markets, where the prices of rice, vegetables, fish, eggs and poultry continue to edge higher.
After visiting several kitchen markets across Dhaka on Saturday, it was found that, except for a few varieties, almost all vegetables were selling for around Tk100 per kg, while green chilli prices had soared to Tk400 per kg.
Rice prices have also resumed their upward trend, with polao rice registering the sharpest increase. Traders said its price has jumped by Tk50–60 per kg within just a few days, adding to the burden on consumers already coping with a gas supply crisis.
According to traders, persistent rainfall and flooding in several parts of the country have submerged vegetable and chilli fields, disrupted supplies and increased transportation costs. The seasonal decline in supply during the monsoon has also contributed to higher prices of most essential commodities.
Fish prices have risen by Tk20–30 per kg over the past week. Pangas is now selling at Tk250 per kg, telapia at Tk280, rui at Tk300–450, pabda at Tk350–400, shrimp at Tk800–1,400, tengra at Tk700, indigenous koi at Tk700–800 and shoal at Tk700 per kg. Prices of bhetki, mrigel, baim, shing and poa fish have also increased.
Hilsa is being sold at Tk1,600–3,200 per kg, depending on its size and quality, while prices of sea fish have also climbed beyond the reach of many middle- and low-income consumers.
Anwar Hossain, a fish vendor at Dhupkhola Kitchen Market, said adverse weather has kept many fishing trawlers from going to sea, while supplies from different parts of the country have declined.
"Wholesale prices have increased due to lower supply, and that has inevitably pushed up retail prices," he said.
Consumers say persistently high food prices are forcing them to rethink their spending, with fish and meat becoming increasingly unaffordable.
"My children wanted to eat fish, but I was shocked by the prices at the market," said shopper Jony Sheikh. "I somehow managed to buy one fish for them. If prices keep rising, we'll have to cut back on fish and meat."
Green chilli prices have surged to Tk400 per kg across Dhaka's kitchen markets, up by around Tk100 from a week ago. Retailers are charging Tk40 for 100 grams and Tk100 for 250 grams.
Locally produced onions have also become costlier, rising by Tk15–20 per kg over the past one-and-a-half to two weeks. Depending on quality, they are now selling for Tk55–65 per kg.
Vegetable prices remain high, with long brinjal selling for Tk120–150 per kg, round brinjal Tk180, white brinjal Tk140, bitter gourd Tk120–140, yardlong beans Tk110–130, snake gourd Tk90–100 and taro corms Tk80–100 per kg. Only sponge gourd and pointed gourd offered some relief, with prices easing to Tk60–80 per kg. Rafique, a vegetable vendor, blamed the price hike on supply shortages caused by heavy rains and flooding.
"Supplies from different parts of the country have declined during the monsoon, while waterlogging has damaged chilli fields in major producing areas. Reduced supply has pushed up prices," he said.
Sridevi Biswas, a shopper at Ray Saheb Bazar, said she had planned to buy several vegetables but returned home with only one.
"I came to buy a few vegetables, but after seeing the prices I bought only one. If this trend continues, it will become even harder for middle-income families to manage their household expenses," she said. Egg prices have also moved up, with farm eggs now selling for Tk145–155 per dozen, compared with Tk135–140 a week ago.
Poultry prices also increased over the past day. Broiler chicken is now selling for Tk190–200 per kg, up from Tk180, while Sonali chicken has risen to Tk340–350 per kg from Tk330–340.
Robin Hasan, a university student living in a shared accommodation, said eggs and chicken had long been the most affordable protein options.
"Even those are becoming more expensive now. Managing within a limited budget is getting harder every day," he said.
While prices of coarse, medium-grade and Miniket rice have remained largely stable, polao rice has seen a sharp spike.
Coarse rice is selling for Tk58–65 per kg, medium-grade rice for Tk68–78, and Miniket and Nazirshail varieties for Tk80–95 per kg.
In contrast, polao rice, which sold for Tk120–140 per kg just a few days ago, is now priced at Tk180–200 per kg, marking an increase of Tk50–60 per kg.
Traders said the jump is the steepest increase in the rice market in recent weeks, adding to the financial strain on consumers already grappling with the rising cost of living.

item.title: NCP leader suspended over remarks about PM Tarique
item.description:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) has handed a fresh suspension to its central committee joint member secretary, Gazi Salahuddin Tanvir, days after he posted objectionable comments about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on social media.
Tanvir was given a temporary suspension from his organizational post and served a show-cause notice on Friday night, hours after his controversial Facebook post drew widespread criticism.
He has been asked to submit a written defense, along with evidence and explanations, to the party's central disciplinary committee within two working days of receiving the notice, explaining why further organizational action should not be taken against him.
The post in question referenced attacks on and obstruction of NCP marches in three districts of Sylhet division, including Habiganj, in which Tanvir accused leaders of Chhatradal and Jubo Dal of involvement.
In the same post, he made the objectionable remarks about the prime minister. He deleted the post a few hours later amid backlash on Facebook, but screenshots of it continued to circulate on social media.
In a letter to Tanvir published on NCP's verified Facebook page Friday night, the party said a comment attributed to him was found to constitute "a serious organizational breach of discipline and damaging the party's image on social media."
The letter added that, given the gravity of the matter, he was being immediately relieved of his organizational responsibilities on the directives of NCP convener Nahid Islam and member secretary Akhter Hossen.
This marks the second time Tanvir has been suspended from the party. He was first removed in April 2025 following allegations that he interfered in deputy commissioner appointments after entering the secretariat in the aftermath of the July mass uprising and that he was involved in commission dealings related to textbook printing contracts with the National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB).
He remained outside the party for about a year before being reinstated on April 16 this year. His latest suspension comes roughly three and a half months after his return.
Shortly after the controversy broke, Tanvir posted on his own Facebook account expressing regret over his remarks.

item.title: Bangladesh's Sundarbans trail global tiger recovery
item.description:
The global wild tiger population is rebounding after decades of decline, driven by stronger conservation efforts and international cooperation. But conservationists say Bangladesh's Sundarbans, home to the country's only wild tiger population, faces unique ecological constraints that make rapid population growth far more difficult than in countries such as India and Nepal.
More than a century ago, an estimated 100,000 wild tigers roamed forests across Asia. By 2010, habitat destruction, poaching and the illegal wildlife trade had reduced that number to around 3,200, prompting the world's 13 tiger range countries to launch the ambitious TX2 initiative at the St. Petersburg Tiger Summit to double global tiger numbers.
According to the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), the Global Tiger Forum (GTF) and national wildlife authorities, the global wild tiger population has now recovered to an estimated 5,500–5,800 animals.
India remains the global leader in tiger conservation, hosting nearly three-quarters of the world's wild tigers. Its tiger population has risen from 1,411 in 2006 to more than 3,680, supported by protected reserves, connected wildlife corridors, intensive anti-poaching operations and sustained government investment.
Nepal has also emerged as one of the world's leading tiger conservation success stories. Its latest National Tiger Census, released on Global Tiger Day, recorded 429 wild tigers—up from 121 in 2009—following years of habitat restoration, scientific monitoring and community-based conservation across the Terai Arc Landscape.
Bangladesh's only wild tiger population survives in the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest shared with India.
Government camera-trap surveys have shown the country's tiger population increasing from 106 in 2015 to 114 in 2018 and an estimated 125 in 2024.
While the upward trend reflects progress in conservation efforts, experts caution against directly comparing Bangladesh's numbers with those of India or Nepal.
Dr Md Anwarul Islam, a wildlife conservationist and former professor of Zoology at the University of Dhaka, said the increase is encouraging but limited by the ecological characteristics of the Sundarbans.
"Our tiger population has increased from 106 in 2015 to 125 in 2024. This is undoubtedly positive, but the increase is modest compared with India, Nepal or Bhutan," he told Dhaka Tribune .
"The Sundarbans is a unique mangrove ecosystem. Unlike large inland forests, its ecological carrying capacity does not allow rapid expansion of tiger populations."
Unlike inland forests with abundant prey and expansive habitats, the Sundarbans can support only a limited number of tigers because of its mangrove ecosystem, experts say.
Islam said several human-induced pressures continue to weaken the forest's ecological balance.
"Illegal hunting of spotted deer, poisoning rivers and canals to catch fish, unsustainable extraction of forest resources and various human disturbances are reducing prey availability and affecting the habitat. Under these conditions, tiger reproduction cannot increase significantly."
He added that neighboring countries benefit from larger and better-connected forest landscapes that naturally support higher tiger populations.
"India, Nepal and Bhutan have larger landscapes and more favorable ecological conditions for tiger conservation. Those environmental advantages play a critical role in supporting larger tiger populations."
Islam said climate change poses an additional long-term threat to tiger conservation in the Sundarbans.
He noted that comparisons with India's overall tiger population can be misleading because the adjoining Indian Sundarbans have experienced similar ecological constraints.
"Many people compare Bangladesh's tiger population with India's national figures. However, if we specifically look at the Indian Sundarbans adjoining Bangladesh, tiger numbers have not increased dramatically there either."
"The two parts of the Sundarbans share similar challenges, including climate change, salinity intrusion, changing prey dynamics and other ecological pressures."
Scientists warn that rising sea levels, stronger cyclones, coastal erosion and increasing salinity are expected to reshape the Sundarbans ecosystem over the coming decades, making long-term tiger conservation increasingly challenging.
While India and Nepal have recorded significant gains, other tiger range countries present a mixed picture.
Russia has increased its Amur tiger population from around 40–50 animals in the 1940s to about 750 today. Bhutan's tiger population has grown from 103 in 2015 to more than 131, while Indonesia's Sumatra supports around 600 Sumatran tigers. Thailand is estimated to have between 180 and 220 wild tigers.
Elsewhere, however, tiger numbers continue to decline. Malaysia's population has fallen from nearly 3,000 several decades ago to fewer than 150 today. Myanmar is estimated to have only 20–30 wild tigers, while Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam have effectively lost their breeding tiger populations.
Conservationists say protecting tigers is about far more than increasing population numbers. As an apex predator, the tiger serves as an indicator of forest health, and safeguarding its habitat also protects biodiversity, freshwater resources and the livelihoods of millions of people who depend on forests.
For Bangladesh, experts say the long-term future of the Royal Bengal Tiger will depend not only on maintaining anti-poaching efforts but also on restoring prey populations, reducing human pressure, strengthening climate resilience and preserving the ecological integrity of the Sundarbans.
"The tiger is an umbrella species," Islam said. "If we can protect the tiger, we protect the entire Sundarbans ecosystem. The future of the tiger is inseparable from the future of the forest itself."

item.title: PM seeks stronger public-private partnership to boost economy
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday expressed optimism that Bangladesh's economy could undergo a positive transformation within the next 4-5 years if the government and the private sector work together to address existing challenges.
Speaking at an interactive session with private sector entrepreneurs, the prime minister said: "There are problems in some areas, but if we work together, we can overcome them."
The nearly 4-hour meeting began around 10am at the Prime Minister's Office in Tejgaon. It was organized by the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA), according to Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
According to Shiplu, the discussions focused on business expansion, attracting greater foreign investment and creating a more conducive environment for industrialization.

item.title: Four killed in pickup-truck collision in Bogra
item.description:
Four people, including a pickup van driver, were killed in a head-on collision between a pickup van and a goods-laden truck in Bogra's Kahaloo upazila on Saturday morning.
The accident occurred in the Kazipara Boubazar area of Birkedar union along the Bogra–Naogaon highway.
The deceased were identified as Toriqul Islam Riyad, 23, son of Ferdous Islam of Pachashi village in Gouripur upazila; pickup driver Nasir Uddin, 24, son of the late Amin Khan of the same village; Lutfor Rahman, 50, son of Toyeb Ali of Raghabpur in Mymensingh Sadar; and Shubha Debnath, 23, son of Chittaranjan Debnath of the same area.
According to family members, the three fish traders had travelled from Mymensingh to Adamdighi in Bogra with a consignment of fish fry for sale. After selling the fish, they were returning home when the accident occurred.
Police said the crash occurred around 10:00 am when the pickup van attempted to overtake a bus and collided head-on with a Naogaon-bound truck coming from the opposite direction, killing the driver and three fish traders on the spot.
The accident briefly disrupted traffic on the Bogra–Naogaon highway. Fire Service and Civil Defence personnel, assisted by police, recovered the bodies and removed the wrecked vehicles, allowing traffic to resume.
Sub-Inspector Brojer Mahato of Kahaloo Police Station said the victims included three fish traders and the pickup driver. The pickup van and the truck have been seized, while the truck driver and his assistant fled the scene.
"The victims' families in Mymensingh have been informed. The bodies will be handed over to their relatives upon arrival," he said.
Officer-in-Charge (OC) Shafiqul Islam said a case has been filed under the Road Transport Act, and efforts are underway to arrest the absconding truck driver.

item.title: Dengue cases rise by 371 in 24 hours
item.description:
Health authorities on Saturday reported 371 new dengue cases across Bangladesh in the 24 hours preceding Saturday morning, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
According to a DGHS statement, 91 patients were admitted to hospitals in Chittagong division, 69 in Barisal division, 57 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC), 46 in Dhaka division, 34 in Khulna division, 32 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC), 23 in Mymensingh division, 17 in Rajshahi division, and 2 in Sylhet division.
With the latest figures, the country has recorded 15,681 dengue cases and 54 deaths so far this year.
Last year, dengue claimed 413 lives and infected 102,861 people across the country.
In 2024, dengue caused 575 deaths and infected 101,214 people.

item.title: 14,384 primary teachers to join from October
item.description:
The Ministry of Primary and Mass Education has said the joining process for 14,384 recommended assistant teachers for government primary schools will begin within October, ending months of uncertainty over their appointments.
The announcement came after an emergency virtual meeting on teacher recruitment held at the ministry on Saturday, according to a message issued by the ministry the same day.
Primary and Mass Education Secretary Shakhawat Hossain said the government is prioritizing the joining of the 14,384 recommended assistant teachers for primary schools, adding that the process had been delayed due to investigation and procedural complexities.
"The joining process will begin by the upcoming October 30," he said.
More than 175 days have passed since the publication of the final results, yet the 14,384 selected candidates are yet to receive their appointment letters. The candidates had earlier demanded that the joining notification be issued by July 29.
With that deadline passing without any notification, the job aspirants had announced a fresh round of continuous sit-in demonstrations at Shahbagh from Sunday.

item.title: Bangladesh drawn with Sri Lanka, Bhutan in SAFF Championship
item.description:
Hosts Bangladesh have been drawn in Group A alongside Sri Lanka and Bhutan for the 2026 SAFF Championship, with Nepal set to join the group if FIFA lifts its suspension before the tournament.
The draw for the 15th edition of South Asia's premier international football tournament was held in Thimphu, Bhutan, on Saturday.
As hosts, Bangladesh were placed in Group A, while regional powerhouse and defending champions India were seeded separately in Group B as the highest-ranked South Asian nation, ensuring the two sides cannot meet before the knockout stage.
Bangladesh's group currently features Sri Lanka and Bhutan, but SAFF confirmed Nepal will be included if FIFA lifts the suspension on the All Nepal Football Association by September 1. If the ban remains in place, the tournament will proceed with six teams.
Group B comprises defending champions India, the Maldives and Pakistan.
The championship will be staged in Dhaka from November 4 to 17, marking Bangladesh's first time hosting the tournament since 2018. The top two teams from each group will advance to the semi-finals, scheduled for November 14, with the final set for November 17.
Bangladesh will look to end a 23-year wait for their second SAFF title, having lifted the trophy only once in 2003. The hosts are expected to field a strengthened squad featuring expatriate footballers such as Hamza Choudhury and Shamit Shome as they bid to capitalise on home advantage.
The tournament, originally scheduled for 2025, was postponed by a year before SAFF confirmed Bangladesh as the host nation earlier this year.

Celebrated mountaineer Nirmal Purja die in avalanche in Pakistan
item.description:
NEPAL-PAKISTAN/CLIMBERS

Celebrated Nepali climber Nirmal Purja, who set a record for the fastest ascent of the world''s 14 highest mountains, died in an avalanche during an expedition in Pakistan, his company said on Saturday.

“Today it is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal ''Nimsdai'' Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak,” his expedition organising company Elite Exped said in an Instagram post.

“We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive,” it added, without giving details.

Purja, 43, and nine others had been missing since Thursday after being struck by an avalanche on the 8,051-metre (26,414-foot) Broad Peak, the world's 12th-highest mountain, a technically difficult climb in Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan region.

Officials said the bodies of Purja and other climbers were located in a difficult site and had yet to be retrieved.

Purja, who served in the British military with the Gurkhas and later in special forces, completed the record-breaking feat in six months in 2019. He became widely known internationally after the Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, "14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible," was released two years later.

The 10 mountaineers were caught in an avalanche around midday on Thursday. Six of the 10 were Nepalis and the others were from ⁠Pakistan, Oman, the US and China.

Search crews recovered three bodies on Friday.

Chhang Dawa Sherpa, a board director of Seven Summit Treks which had three Sherpa guides among the dead ⁠climbers, said the remaining bodies were "spotted and identified" with the help of drone footage and were yet to be retrieved.

"They are in a difficult spot and have not been retrieved yet," Chhang told Reuters.

He said that unlike Nepal, Pakistan does not have the practice of long-line rescue by helicopters on the mountains.

"We have to take into account the safety of those who go and retrieve the bodies."

Sajid Hussain, deputy director of the tourism department of Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan, said the rescue operation was still ongoing.

"Rescue teams have successfully identified the location of the victims; however, they have not yet been able to recover and bring them down safely," he told Reuters.

"Although the location has been confirmed, the recovery mission has not yet been successful."

Hussain said this is an "extremely challenging" mountain recovery operation that requires rescuers to climb to the site.

While drone surveillance and aerial reconnaissance have helped identify the exact location, reaching the victims and safely recovering them remains a highly difficult task, he said.

In 2019, Purja climbed Annapurna, the 10th-highest mountain in the world. He then began taking on other 8,000-metre peaks. Of the world's 14 highest mountains, eight are in ⁠Nepal, five in Pakistan and one in the Tibet region of China.

Climbing experts say barely more than three dozen mountaineers have climbed all 14 peaks to date. Broad Peak is considered one of Pakistan''s most challenging climbs.
